thm:bounded-residual-parametric-plugin.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M\), a block \(b\), and a pre-block history \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\). The class definition makes the count vector, fitting values, potential outcomes, and residual lists fixed at this node. For an arm \(a\), write
\[
X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad N=n_{nb},\qquad m=m_{nba},
\]
and let \(\mu=N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{X_i}=\mu_{nba}\) and
\(\nu=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i}\). The bounded-residual condition gives
\[
|X_i|\le |R_{nbi}(a)|+|\bar R_{nba}|\le2M.
\tag{1}
\]
Consistency identifies the sampled residuals, and conditional complete randomization makes the arm-\(a\) labels a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m\).

We first prove the required one-dimensional finite-population empirical-measure bound. Let \(F\) and \(\widehat F\) be the distribution functions of \(\mu\) and \(\nu\). For each \(t\in\mathbb R\), the exact inclusion-probability calculation for the finite list \((\mathbf1\{X_i\le t\})_{i=1}^N\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{\widehat F(t)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
=\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}F(t)\{1-F(t)\}\le\frac1{4m}.
\tag{2}
\]
For completeness, for finitely supported probability measures on the line, order all atoms jointly. Across the interval between two consecutive atom locations, every transport plan must move at least the absolute cumulative mass imbalance across that cut. The greedy increasing matching moves exactly that imbalance and no more. Summing interval length times cumulative imbalance proves directly that
\[
W_1(\nu,\mu)=\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F(t)-F(t)|\,dt.
\tag{3}
\]
This is a finite matching identity, not an imported empirical-process theorem. By (1), the integrand in (3) vanishes outside \([-2M,2M]\). Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and (2) therefore give
\[
E\{W_1(\nu,\mu)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le\int_{-2M}^{2M}\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat F(t)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})}\,dt
\le\frac{2M}{\sqrt m}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\bar X_S=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\). Since the population mean of the \(X_i\)'s is zero, the simple-random-sampling covariance identity and (1) imply
\[
E(\bar X_S^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2
\le\frac{8M^2}{m}.
\tag{5}
\]
The observable margin is exactly
\(\widehat\mu_{nba}=T_{-\bar X_S\,\#}\nu\), because subtracting the observed residual mean sends \(X_i\) to \(X_i-\bar X_S\). Coupling every atom with its translate, then using (4), (5), and the triangle inequality, yields the observable-centering bound
\[
E\{W_1(\widehat\mu_{nba},\mu_{nba})\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le (2+2\sqrt2)M m_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]

The sample-variance term has the same parametric order. Put
\[
A_S=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i^2,
\qquad A=\frac1N\sum_iX_i^2.
\]
Since \(0\le X_i^2\le4M^2\), the sampling covariance identity gives
\[
E(|A_S-A|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le\left\{\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)
\frac1{N-1}\sum_i(X_i^2-A)^2\right\}^{1/2}
\le4\sqrt2 M^2m^{-1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
For \(m,N\ge2\),
\[
\widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac{m}{m-1}(A_S-\bar X_S^2),
\qquad S_{nba}^2=\frac{N}{N-1}A.
\]
Using (5), (7), \(m/(m-1)\le2\), \(A\le4M^2\), and
\(|m/(m-1)-N/(N-1)|\le2/m\), we obtain a numerical constant \(C_0\) such that
\[
E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C_0M^2m_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]

We next prove bounded-support Lipschitz sensitivity of the fixed-\(K\) multi-marginal objective. Let \(\phi(x)=(c^\top x)^2\). If \(x,y\in[-2M,2M]^K\), contrast normalization implies \(\|c\|_1\le\sqrt K\) and \(|c_a|\le1\), so
\[
|\phi(x)-\phi(y)|
=|c^\top(x-y)|\,|c^\top(x+y)|
\le4M\sqrt K\sum_{a=1}^K|x_a-y_a|.
\tag{9}
\]
For each arm, take an optimal \(W_1\) coupling between \(\mu_{nba}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\). Glue its conditional kernel to any coupling of the population margins. The resulting vector has the empirical margins, and (9) bounds the change in expected cost by
\[
4M\sqrt K\sum_{a=1}^K W_1(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba}).
\]
Apply this construction to a population minimizer and maximizer and then reverse the roles of the population and empirical margins. The finite coupling polytopes are compact, so all four optimizers exist. Equation (6) thus gives, for either sign, a constant \(C_1=C_1(K,M)\) such that
\[
E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C_1\left(\min_a m_{nba}\right)^{-1/2}.
\tag{10}
\]

Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\). When every arm count is at least two, overlap, count growth, and \((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
&E\bigl[|\widehat L_{nb}-L_{nb}|+|\widehat U_{nb}-U_{nb}|
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\bigr]\\
&\qquad\le
C_2w_{nb}^2\left\{
\sum_a\frac{c_a^2M^2m_{nba}^{-1/2}}{m_{nba}}
+\frac{M^2(\min_am_{nba})^{-1/2}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}\\
&\qquad\le C_3t_{nb}q_n^{-1/2},
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where \(L_{nb},U_{nb},\widehat L_{nb},\widehat U_{nb}\) denote the corresponding block summands in the two envelope definitions. In the last line we used \(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), \(m_{nba}^{-1/2}\le q_n^{-1/2}\), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and absorbed the fixed \(K\) into \(C_3=C_3(K,\varepsilon_0,M)\).

The bound (11) is valid at every pre-block history with the same constant. Summing it, applying the tower property along the original adaptive filtration, and using \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\) gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M}
E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
\le C_Mq_n^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
No maximum over history nodes, union bound, or conditioning on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) occurs. Consequently neither \(B_n\) nor a logarithmic history factor appears, and no block-leverage condition has been used. If an arm count is below two, then \(q_n<2\); since the theorem truncates the normalized loss at one, increasing \(C_M\) by a universal factor covers these finitely indexed convention cases. This proves the displayed theorem for every \(n\). Finally, \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak E_M\) by the two class definitions, so the same bound holds over \(\mathfrak D_M\), and \(q_n\to\infty\) proves uniform convergence on both classes.

snapshot.stmt:
For every fixed \(M>0\), there is a constant \(C_M<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,M\), such that for every \(n\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge
\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]
\le C_Mq_n^{-1/2}.
\]
Consequently the same bound holds with \(\mathfrak E_M\) replaced by the bounded-residual subclass \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak D\), and the normalized endpoint error converges to zero uniformly on either class. The bound has no dependence on \(B_n\), contains no logarithmic history factor, and requires no block-leverage condition. It is unconditional under the original sequential randomization and never freezes the terminal adaptive path.

defs.def:bounded-residual-arrays:
For a fixed \(M>0\), define the optional subclass
\[
\mathfrak D_M=\left\{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)):
\sup_{n\ge1}\max_{b\le B_n}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}
\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\max_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|\le M\right\}.
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak D\); the displayed bound is an additional common history-uniform restriction and does not replace any member property of \(\mathfrak D\).
defs.def:admissible-arrays:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]
defs.def:bounded-residual-endpoint-arrays:
For the endpoint-only rate statement, let \(\mathfrak E_M(K,\varepsilon_0,M,(q_n))\) be the class of the same triangular experiment-analysis arrays for which \(K\) is fixed, \(q_n\to\infty\), the common bound
\[
\sup_{n\ge1}\max_{b\le B_n}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}
\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\max_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|\le M
\]
holds, and the member properties \(\text{ass:fixed-potential-outcomes}\), \(\text{ass:consistency-no-interference}\), \(\text{ass:predictable-counts}\), \(\text{ass:complete-block-randomization}\), \(\text{ass:predictable-adjustment}\), \(\text{ass:overlap}\), \(\text{ass:contrast-zero-sum}\), \(\text{ass:contrast-normalization}\), and \(\text{ass:growing-arm-counts}\) hold with the displayed common parameters. No residual-moment, block-leverage, or predictable-quadratic-variation condition is included in \(\mathfrak E_M\). By construction, \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak E_M\).
defs.def:observed-residual-margins:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).
defs.def:plugin-envelope: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]

assumptions.ass:complete-block-randomization: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-potential-outcomes: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
assumptions.ass:growing-arm-counts: The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).
assumptions.ass:overlap: The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-adjustment: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-counts: The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:block-leverage: The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
assumptions.ass:residual-moments: The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
assumptions.ass:qv-growth: The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).

The bound (11) is valid at every pre-block history with the same constant. Summing it, applying the tower property along the original adaptive filtration, and using \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\) gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak E_M}
E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
\le C_Mq_n^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
No maximum over history nodes, union bound, or conditioning on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) occurs. Consequently neither \(B_n\) nor a logarithmic history factor appears, and no block-leverage condition has been used. If an arm count is below two, then \(q_n<2\); since the theorem truncates the normalized loss at one, increasing \(C_M\) by a universal factor covers these finitely indexed convention cases. This proves the displayed theorem for every \(n\). Finally, \(\mathfrak D_M\subseteq\mathfrak E_M\) by the two class definitions, so the same bound holds over \(\mathfrak D_M\), and \(q_n\to\infty\) proves uniform convergence on both classes.

lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation.proof_tex:
Put \(X_{nb}=D_{nb}/\sigma_n\), and define the predictable quantities
\[
v_{nb}=E(X_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}),\qquad
A_{nj}=\sum_{b=1}^jv_{nb},
\]
\[
\lambda_{nb}(e)=E\{X_{nb}^2\mathbf 1(|X_{nb}|>e)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\},
\qquad \Lambda_{nj}(e)=\sum_{b=1}^j\lambda_{nb}(e).
\tag{1}
\]
Then \(A_{nB_n}=V_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) in probability, and the displayed Lindeberg hypothesis says that \(\Lambda_{nB_n}(e)\to0\) in probability for each fixed \(e>0\).

We first turn these two convergences into bounded predictable budgets. There are deterministic sequences \(e_n\downarrow0\) and \(d_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
\Pr\{|A_{nB_n}-1|>d_n\}+\Pr\{\Lambda_{nB_n}(e_n)>d_n\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, for each integer \(k\ge1\), convergence at the fixed threshold \(1/k\) supplies \(N_k\) such that, for \(n\ge N_k\), both probabilities with \(d_n=e_n=1/k\) are at most \(1/k\). Taking \(N_k\) increasing and using these values on \(N_k\le n<N_{k+1}\) proves (2).

For \(b\le B_n\), set
\[
I_{nb}=\mathbf 1\{A_{nb}\le1+d_n,\ \Lambda_{nb}(e_n)\le d_n\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Because \(v_{nb}\) and \(\lambda_{nb}(e_n)\) are \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable, \(I_{nb}\) is predictable. Both cumulative processes in (1) are nondecreasing, so the indices for which \(I_{nb}=1\) form an initial segment and
\[
\sum_b I_{nb}v_{nb}\le1+d_n,qquad
\sum_b I_{nb}\lambda_{nb}(e_n)\le d_n.
\tag{4}
\]
Define the stopped, truncated, conditionally recentered differences
\[
Y_{nb}=I_{nb}\left[X_{nb}\mathbf 1\{|X_{nb}|\le e_n\}
-E\{X_{nb}\mathbf 1(|X_{nb}|\le e_n)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\right]
\tag{5}
\]
and \(u_{nb}=E(Y_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\), \(B_n^Y=\sum_bu_{nb}\). The variables \(Y_{nb}\) are martingale differences and satisfy \(|Y_{nb}|\le2e_n\). Moreover, (4) gives
\[
0\le B_n^Y\lesum_bI_{nb}v_{nb}\le1+d_n.
\tag{6}
\]

Let
\[
G_n=\{|A_{nB_n}-1|\le d_n,\ \Lambda_{nB_n}(e_n)\le d_n\}.
\]
On \(G_n\), every \(I_{nb}\) equals one. Since \(E(X_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=0\), if
\(r_{nb}=E\{X_{nb}\mathbf 1(|X_{nb}|\le e_n)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\), then
\[
r_{nb}=-E\{X_{nb}\mathbf 1(|X_{nb}|>e_n)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\},
\qquad r_{nb}^2\le\lambda_{nb}(e_n).
\tag{7}
\]
Consequently, on \(G_n\),
\[
0\le A_{nB_n}-B_n^Y
=\sum_b\{\lambda_{nb}(e_n)+r_{nb}^2\}
\le2d_n,
\tag{8}
\]
and hence \(|B_n^Y-1|\le3d_n\). Equations (2), (6), and (8) imply
\[
B_n^Y\to1\quad\hbox{in probability},qquad E|B_n^Y-1|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{9}
\]
The second conclusion follows because \(0\le B_n^Y\le1+d_n\), so the sequence is uniformly bounded.

The truncation does not alter the normalized sum asymptotically. Put
\[
Q_{nb}=I_{nb}\left[X_{nb}\mathbf 1\{|X_{nb}|>e_n\}
-E\{X_{nb}\mathbf 1(|X_{nb}|>e_n)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\right].
\]
The \(Q_{nb}\)'s are martingale differences, and by (4), orthogonality of martingale differences, and conditional variance bounded by conditional second moment,
\[
E\left(\sum_bQ_{nb}\right)^2
=E\sum_bE(Q_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le E\sum_bI_{nb}\lambda_{nb}(e_n)\le d_n.
\tag{10}
\]
On \(G_n\), \(\sum_b(X_{nb}-Y_{nb})=\sum_bQ_{nb}\). Thus, for every \(\eta>0\), (2), (10), and Chebyshev's inequality yield
\[
\Pr\left\{\left|\sum_bX_{nb}-\sum_bY_{nb}\right|>\eta\right\}
\le\Pr(G_n^c)+d_n\eta^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{11}
\]

It remains to derive the Gaussian limit for the bounded array in (5). We give the characteristic-function calculation. Write
\(S_{nj}^Y=\sum_{b=1}^jY_{nb}\) and \(B_{nj}^Y=\sum_{b=1}^ju_{nb}\). For fixed \(t\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
H_{nj}=\exp\{itS_{nj}^Y+t^2B_{nj}^Y/2\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Taylor's formula with remainder gives, conditionally on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\),
\[
E(e^{itY_{nb}}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=1-\frac{t^2u_{nb}}2+R_{nb},qquad
|R_{nb}|\le\frac{|t|^3}{6}E(|Y_{nb}|^3\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le\frac{|t|^3}{3}e_nu_{nb}.
\tag{13}
\]
Because \(|Y_{nb}|\le2e_n\), one also has \(u_{nb}\le4e_n^2\). Expanding \(e^{t^2u_{nb}/2}\) to first order and using (13), there is a finite constant \(C_t\), independent of \(n,b\), such that
\[
\left|e^{t^2u_{nb}/2}E(e^{itY_{nb}}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})-1\right|
\le C_t(e_nu_{nb}+u_{nb}^2).
\tag{14}
\]
By (6), \(|H_{n,b-1}|\le\exp\{t^2(1+d_n)/2\}\). Taking conditional expectations in (12), telescoping expectations, and applying (6), (14), and
\(\sum_bu_{nb}^2\le4e_n^2\sum_bu_{nb}\), we obtain
\[
|E H_{nB_n}-1|
\le C_t'(e_n+e_n^2)(1+d_n)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{15}
\]
On the other hand, (6) and (9) imply
\[
E\left|e^{-t^2B_n^Y/2}-e^{-t^2/2}\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Since \(e^{itS_{nB_n}^Y}=H_{nB_n}e^{-t^2B_n^Y/2}\), the uniform modulus bound following (12), together with (15)--(16), gives
\[
E e^{itS_{nB_n}^Y}\longrightarrow e^{-t^2/2}
\quad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb R.
\tag{17}
\]
The right side is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). The cited \(\text{lem:levy-continuity-criterion}\) applied to (17) yields
\(\sum_bY_{nb}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\). Finally, (11) and the elementary continuity argument
\[
\Pr\{S_n^Y\le x-\eta\}-\Pr\{|S_n^X-S_n^Y|>\eta\}
\le\Pr\{S_n^X\le x\}
\le\Pr\{S_n^Y\le x+\eta\}+\Pr\{|S_n^X-S_n^Y|>\eta\}
\]
at continuity points of the Gaussian distribution show that
\[
\sum_bX_{nb}=\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_bD_{nb}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
This proof uses the Lindeberg threshold \(\epsilon\sigma_n\) exactly as displayed in the statement.

thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necess.proof_tex:
Fix the core's \(K\ge2\) and normalized zero-sum contrast \(c\). We construct a nonadaptive triangular array. Let
\[
B_n=n,qquad q_n=2n,qquad n_{nb}=Kq_n,qquad
m_{nba}=q_n,qquad w_{nb}=B_n^{-1},qquad g_{nbi}(a)=0.
\tag{1}
\]
In every block and every arm use the same fixed list: for exactly \(Kq_n/2=Kn\) common unit labels set \(Y_{nbi}(a)=1\), and for the remaining \(Kn\) labels set \(Y_{nbi}(a)=-1\). Independently across blocks, draw uniformly from assignments realizing the quotas in (1). This is a history-independent special case of predictable complete-block randomization and is one globally consistent fixed-potential-outcome completion.

Every arm list has mean zero and finite-population variance
\[
S_n^2=\frac{Kq_n}{Kq_n-1}.
\tag{2}
\]
The residuals equal the outcomes and are bounded by one, so their \((4+\delta_0)\)-moment average is one. Also \(p_{nba}=1/K\), which satisfies
\(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) for every fixed
\(\varepsilon_0\in(0,1/K)\). Thus the fixed-outcome, consistency, predictable-count, complete-randomization, predictable-adjustment, overlap, contrast, residual-moment, and growing-count conditions hold with common constants, for example \(C_R=1\). Moreover,
\[
s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}}
=\frac1{B_nKq_n},qquad
\frac{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}}{s_n^2}=\frac1{B_n}.
\tag{3}
\]
Hence block leverage holds with \(\ell_n=B_n^{-1}\to0\).

At each block the common labels couple the centered arm coordinates as \((X,\ldots,X)\), with the common centered marginal. Since \(\sum_ac_a=0\), this feasible coupling has cost
\[
\left(\sum_ac_aX\right)^2=X^2\left(\sum_ac_a\right)^2=0.
\tag{4}
\]
Every quadratic cost is nonnegative, so \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\), and the true fixed-potential-outcome coupling is the zero-cost coupling (4). The conditional-variance identity in
\(\text{thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope}\), followed by \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), gives
\[
E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=w_{nb}^2\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_n^2}{q_n}
=\frac{w_{nb}^2S_n^2}{q_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
The upper endpoint has the same diagonal term and subtracts
\(J_{nb}^{-}/(n_{nb}-1)=0\). Therefore
\[
V_n=U_n=\frac{S_n^2}{B_nq_n},qquad
\frac{V_n}{s_n^2}=KS_n^2\ge K.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus QV growth holds, for instance with \(v_0=1\), and QV stabilization holds identically because \(V_n=E(V_n)\) is deterministic.

The smallest exact stress test is the case \(K=2\), one block, \(q_n=2\), common list
\((-1,-1,1,1)\), and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\). Across all six equiprobable assignments of two labels to arm one, its sample mean is \(-1,0,1\) with multiplicities \(1,4,1\), and the complementary arm mean is its negative. Thus \(D_{n1}\) is
\(-\sqrt2w_{n1},0,\sqrt2w_{n1}\) with probabilities \(1/6,4/6,1/6\), and
\[
E(D_{n1})=0,qquad E(D_{n1}^2)=\frac{2w_{n1}^2}{3}
=\frac{w_{n1}^2}{2}\frac43.
\tag{7}
\]
Since \(S_n^2=4/3\), (7) exactly equals (5); exhaustive enumeration detects neither bias nor a variance-formula failure.

The sharpened \(\text{thm:history-uniform-plugin}\) applies to this common-parameter array and gives
\[
\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{8}
\]
Since (6) has \(U_n/s_n^2=KS_n^2\ge K\),
\[
\frac{\widehat U_n}{U_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{9}
\]

We verify the CLT primitives rather than assuming a limit law. For a uniform size-\(q_n\) subset \(S\) of a centered list \((x_i)_{i=1}^{Kq_n}\), put \(A_r=\sum_i|x_i|^r\) and
\(\pi_r=(q_n)_r/(Kq_n)_r\). Expanding by equality patterns, exactly as in the fourth-moment calculation for simple random sampling, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
={}&\pi_1A_4-4\pi_2A_4+3\pi_2(A_2^2-A_4)\\
&+6\pi_3(2A_4-A_2^2)+\pi_4(3A_2^2-6A_4).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
For the present \(\{-1,1\}\) list, \(A_2=A_4=Kq_n\) and \(\pi_r\le K^{-r}\). Dividing by \(q_n^4\), then using
\(|\sum_ac_ax_a|^4\le K\sum_a|x_a|^4\), gives a constant \(C_K<\infty\) such that
\[
E(D_{nb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\le C_Kw_{nb}^4q_n^{-2}.
\tag{11}
\]
This calculation uses only marginal fourth moments and therefore does not assume independence among the arm sample means. With \(\sigma_n^2=V_n=S_n^2/(B_nq_n)>0\), for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac1{\sigma_n^2}\sum_bE\{D_{nb}^2\mathbf1(|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_n)
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\\
&\quad\le\frac1{\epsilon^2\sigma_n^4}\sum_bE(D_{nb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le\frac{C_K}{\epsilon^2B_n(S_n^2)^2}\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
The martingale property follows from the exact-envelope theorem, and QV stabilization follows from (6). The proved
\(\text{lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation}\) now yields
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{U_n}}
=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{13}
\]
The causal estimand is \(\tau_n=0\) on this witness because the potential outcomes agree across arms pointwise and \(\sum_ac_a=0\); it remains a finite-population causal contrast, not a transport functional.

Fix \(\rho\in(0,1)\), \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and write \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\). For \(0<\eta<1\), on
\(\{|\widehat U_n/U_n-1|\le\eta\}\) the random threshold below lies between the thresholds obtained from \(1-\eta\) and \(1+\eta\). Equations (9), (13), and continuity of the Gaussian distribution give, first as \(n\to\infty\) and then as \(\eta\downarrow0\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|
\le z\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}\\
&\quad=\Pr\left\{
\left|\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{U_n}}\right|
\le z\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n/U_n}\right\}\\
&\quad\longrightarrow2\Phi\left(z\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
Because \(z>0\) and \(0<1-\rho<1\), one has \(z\sqrt{1-\rho}<z\). The standard normal density is strictly positive, so
\[
\Phi(z)-\Phi(z\sqrt{1-\rho})
=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{z\sqrt{1-\rho}}^z e^{-u^2/2}\,du>0.
\]
Hence the limit in (14) is strictly smaller than \(2\Phi(z)-1=1-\alpha\). If a broader design family contains this subclass, its worst-case coverage is no larger than the coverage of this displayed member for every \(n\); taking the upper limit proves the asserted certificate. The witness is nonadaptive and globally consistent, so the argument never selects incompatible optimizers at different adaptive-history nodes.

snapshot.stmt:
There exists a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass of an admissible common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) with \(B_n\to\infty\), \(q_n\to\infty\), equal block weights \(w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}\), block sizes \(n_{nb}=Kq_n\), equal quotas \(m_{nba}=q_n\), zero adjustments \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), and identical bounded potential-outcome lists across arms, such that \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\) in every block and \(V_n=U_n\) deterministically. This subclass satisfies the full overlap, residual-moment, count-growth, block-leverage, predictable-QV growth, predictable-QV stabilization, endpoint-consistency, and martingale-CLT conditions. Consequently, for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1
 <1-\alpha.
\]
Therefore, for any broader design family containing this subclass, the limsup of its worst-case coverage after replacing \(\widehat U_n\) by \((1-\rho)\widehat U_n\) is at most the displayed strict sub-nominal limit. This is a fixed-quota subclass converse for uniform inference, not a claim that independently selected nodewise transport optimizers are jointly realizable by one completion over an adaptive history tree.

defs.def:admissible-arrays:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]
defs.def:plugin-envelope: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]
defs.def:observed-residual-margins:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).

assumptions.ass:complete-block-randomization: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).
assumptions.ass:qv-stabilization: For every \(\eta>0\), the predictable quadratic variation stabilizes at its deterministic design expectation uniformly over the common-parameter class: \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\left|\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}-1\right|>\eta\right)\longrightarrow0.\]
assumptions.ass:fixed-potential-outcomes: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
assumptions.ass:predictable-counts: The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-adjustment: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:overlap: The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
assumptions.ass:growing-arm-counts: The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).
assumptions.ass:block-leverage: The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
assumptions.ass:residual-moments: The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).

node.statement:
There exists a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass of an admissible common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) with \(B_n\to\infty\), \(q_n\to\infty\), equal block weights \(w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}\), block sizes \(n_{nb}=Kq_n\), equal quotas \(m_{nba}=q_n\), zero adjustments \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), and identical bounded potential-outcome lists across arms, such that \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\) in every block and \(V_n=U_n\) deterministically. This subclass satisfies the full overlap, residual-moment, count-growth, block-leverage, predictable-QV growth, predictable-QV stabilization, endpoint-consistency, and martingale-CLT conditions. Consequently, for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1
 <1-\alpha.
\]
Therefore, for any broader design family containing this subclass, the limsup of its worst-case coverage after replacing \(\widehat U_n\) by \((1-\rho)\widehat U_n\) is at most the displayed strict sub-nominal limit. This is a fixed-quota subclass converse for uniform inference, not a claim that independently selected nodewise transport optimizers are jointly realizable by one completion over an adaptive history tree.
node.justification: An explicit admissible fixed-quota sequence makes the transport upper endpoint equal the true predictable quadratic variation and supplies a matching fixed-fraction undercoverage certificate.
node.gap: Nodewise completion attainability is not needed for this inference converse; the remaining unsolved issue is simultaneous compatibility across an adaptive history tree.
node.consumer: The result certifies that a batched quota-controlled trial cannot uniformly shorten the transport-based standard error by any fixed fraction, even on the simplest nonadaptive subfamily.

thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(b\), condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), and abbreviate
\[
N=n_{nb},\qquad m_a=m_{nba},\qquad p_a=m_a/N,
\qquad R_i(a)=R_{nbi}(a),\qquad x_i(a)=R_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}.
\tag{1}
\]
The divisions are valid because \(1\le m_a\le N-1\), hence \(N\ge2\). By \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}adjustment}\), the residual lists in (1) are fixed under this conditioning; by \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}counts}\), so are the counts.

We first verify unconditional square integrability, rather than infer it merely from conditional finite support. Put \(p=4+\delta_0>4\). The moment condition \(\mathrm{ass:residual\text{-}moments}\) and the power-mean inequality give, almost surely at every pre-block history,
\[
\frac1N\sum_i|R_i(a)|
\le\left\{\frac1N\sum_i|R_i(a)|^p\right\}^{1/p}
\le C_R^{1/p}.
\tag{2}
\]
For every realized assignment,
\[
\left|\frac1{m_a}\sum_i\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}R_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right|
\le\left(\frac N{m_a}+1\right)C_R^{1/p}
\le(N+1)C_R^{1/p}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{def:block\text{-}martingale}\) implies the deterministic almost-sure bound
\[
|D_{nb}|\le w_{nb}\|c\|_1(N+1)C_R^{1/p}<\infty.
\tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(n,b\), the right side is finite, so \(E(D_{nb}^2)<\infty\). This is the required unconditional square integrability.

Let \(I_i^a=\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}\). Complete-block randomization gives
\[
E(I_i^a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=\frac{m_a}{N}=p_a.
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently, (5) and \(\mathrm{def:block\text{-}martingale}\) give
\[
E(D_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=w_{nb}\sum_ac_a\left\{\frac1{m_a}\sum_i p_aR_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
The increment \(D_{nb}\) is measurable after block \(b\) is assigned. Hence (4)--(6) prove that \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a square-integrable martingale with differences \(D_{nb}\).

For distinct unit labels \(i\ne k\), the same complete-randomization law gives
\[
E(I_i^aI_k^a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{m_a(m_a-1)}{N(N-1)},
\qquad
E(I_i^aI_k^{a'}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{m_am_{a'}}{N(N-1)}\quad(a\ne a'),
\tag{7}
\]
whereas \(I_i^aI_i^{a'}=0\) for \(a\ne a'\). Since \(\sum_i x_i(a)=0\), expansion of the diagonal and distinct-label terms in (7) yields
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1{m_a}\sum_iI_i^aR_i(a)\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
=\left(\frac1{m_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2.
\tag{8}
\]
For \(a\ne a'\), use
\(\sum_{i\ne k}x_i(a)x_k(a')=-\sum_i x_i(a)x_i(a')\) in (7) to obtain
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\frac1{m_a}\sum_iI_i^aR_i(a),
\frac1{m_{a'}}\sum_iI_i^{a'}R_i(a')\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
=-\frac{S_{nb,aa'}}N,
\tag{9}
\]
where
\[
S_{nb,aa'}=\frac1{N-1}\sum_i x_i(a)x_i(a').
\]
Combining (8)--(9) and expanding the contrast square gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})}{w_{nb}^2}
&=\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
-\frac1N\left\{\sum_ac_a^2S_{nba}^2+2\sum_{a<a'}c_ac_{a'}S_{nb,aa'}\right\}\\
&=\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
-\frac1{N(N-1)}\sum_i\left\{\sum_ac_ax_i(a)\right\}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Define the common-label centered law
\[
\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}
=\frac1N\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\delta_{(x_i(1),\ldots,x_i(K))}.
\tag{11}
\]
Its arm-\(a\) marginal is \(\mu_{nba}\), so \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\). Substitution of (11) into (10) proves
\[
E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}
-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\}.
\tag{12}
\]

Fix \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\). Each margin \(\mu_{nba}^h\) has finite support. The product measure shows that \(\Gamma_{nb}^h\) is nonempty. In its finite coordinate representation, the marginal equalities and nonnegativity constraints make it closed, while all coordinates lie in \([0,1]\), so it is compact. The quadratic cost is a continuous linear functional of the coupling coordinates. It therefore attains its minimum \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\) and maximum \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\); convexity of the transportation polytope and linearity show that the full image is the interval between these extrema. Because the cost coefficient in (12) is \(-w_{nb}^2/(n_{nb}-1)<0\), the lower conditional-variance endpoint uses \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\), the upper endpoint uses \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), and each is attained in \(\Gamma_{nb}^h\).

Both endpoints are nonnegative. Indeed, set \(p_{nba}^h=m_{nba}^h/n_{nb}\). Positivity of the nodewise counts and \(\sum_ap_{nba}^h=1\) allow Cauchy--Schwarz to give, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^K\),
\[
\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2
=\left(\sum_a\frac{c_ax_a}{\sqrt{p_{nba}^h}}\sqrt{p_{nba}^h}\right)^2
\le\sum_a\frac{c_a^2x_a^2}{p_{nba}^h}.
\tag{13}
\]
The definition of the centered empirical marginal gives
\[
\int x_a^2d\mu_{nba}^h(x_a)
=\frac{n_{nb}-1}{n_{nb}}(S_{nba}^h)^2.
\tag{14}
\]
Therefore every \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^h\) satisfies
\[
\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma
\le\sum_a\frac{c_a^2(S_{nba}^h)^2}{m_{nba}^h},
\tag{15}
\]
which proves the assertion.

By \(\mathrm{def:history\text{-}tree\text{-}rectangular\text{-}relaxation}\), the coupling coordinate at each history node may be chosen independently. On a fixed root-to-leaf path, the Minkowski sum of the visited nodewise variance intervals is the interval whose endpoints are the sums of the respective nodewise endpoints. Choosing an optimizer at each visited node attains both summed endpoints within \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). At every actually visited node, (11) is feasible. Summing (12) over the visited blocks and applying \(\mathrm{def:qv\text{-}envelope}\) gives the predictable pathwise containment
\[
V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\in[L_n,U_n].
\tag{16}
\]
Every summand and endpoint in (16) is measurable before its block is randomized. Thus no step conditions on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\), and the argument establishes exactness only nodewise and path by path in the Cartesian convexified relaxation. It does not construct a single globally consistent fixed-potential-outcome completion realizing independently selected optimizers at different history nodes.

The smallest adaptive check makes this filtration point explicit. Take two arms, \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), zero adjustment, and a first block with common arm list \((-1,1)\) and quota \((1,1)\). Its two assignments give \(D_{n1}=\sqrt2w_{n1}\) and \(D_{n1}=-\sqrt2w_{n1}\). In the second block use common list \((-1,0,1)\), choose quota \((1,2)\) after the positive first-block value, and quota \((2,1)\) after the negative value. With \(d=3w_{n2}/(2\sqrt2)\), the three equiprobable second-block values are \((-d,0,d)\) after the first history and \((d,0,-d)\) after the second. Hence all six assignment sequences have conditional second-block mean zero and
\[
E(D_{n1}D_{n2})
=E\{D_{n1}E(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\}=0.
\tag{17}
\]
Finally, when \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), the residual lists equal the fixed potential-outcome lists. Direct substitution in (12), followed by optimization over their centered joint coupling, gives the stated static quadratic multi-marginal-transport variance formula.

snapshot.stmt: For every array in \(\mathfrak D\), \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a martingale and \[E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\},\] where \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\) is the joint centered residual coupling in block \(b\). At every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\), the conditional variance range over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) has endpoints obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\) and \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), and both endpoints are attained within that node's convexified coupling set. Evaluating these nodewise endpoints along the realized pre-block histories yields the predictable pathwise containment \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\). For any fixed root-to-leaf path, independent selection of feasible couplings at its visited nodes attains both summed endpoints in the rectangular relaxation \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Thus the interval is exact only nodewise and path by path inside that rectangular convexified relaxation. This theorem does not assert that one globally consistent fixed-potential-outcome adaptive-history completion realizes independently selected optimizers across different nodes. When \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), direct substitution gives the static quadratic MOT variance formula of Gao, Ge, and Qian. When \(B_n\ge2\) and counts respond to earlier outcomes, \([L_n,U_n]\) is a sum of pre-block-measurable random endpoints rather than one static MOT functional, and the claim does not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

defs.def:admissible-arrays:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]
defs.def:history-tree-rectangular-relaxation: For the ex ante history-tree margin system \(\boldsymbol\mu_n=(\mu_{nba}^{h})_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\,a\in\mathcal A}\), set \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}=\Gamma(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h})\), define \[J_{nb}^{h,-}=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\qquad J_{nb}^{h,+}=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\] define \[U_{nb}^{h}=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2}{m_{nba}^{h}}-\frac{J_{nb}^{h,-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\] and let \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\prod_{b=1}^{B_n}\prod_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\). The Cartesian product permits a separate convexified coupling at every history node.

prop:sorting-and-fixed-k-lp.proof_tex:
For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), the identity
\[
\frac12(x-y)^2=\frac12x^2+\frac12y^2-xy
\tag{1}
\]
shows that the two marginal square terms do not depend on the coupling. The cited rearrangement result \(\mathrm{lem:twoarm\text{-}rearrangement\text{-}extrema}\) says that equal-rank pairing maximizes \(E(XY)\), whereas reverse-rank pairing minimizes it. By (1), equal-rank pairing therefore minimizes the quadratic cost and reverse-rank pairing maximizes it. This proves the two formulas in \(\mathrm{def:twoarm\text{-}sorting}\).

For general fixed \(K\), label every atom of every observed empirical margin, even when two labels carry the same numerical residual. A coupling of the labeled empirical measures assigns a mass \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\) to each tuple
\((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\). Its \(a\)-th marginal is \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) if and only if
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}
\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(a\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\). Thus the feasible arrays in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\text{-}k\text{-}lp}\) are exactly all couplings of the empirical margins, and the displayed LP objective is exactly
\[
\int\left(\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the product coupling, and it is a compact polytope because (2), nonnegativity, and total mass one define a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space. The linear objective consequently attains its minimum and maximum, which are respectively \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) by \(\mathrm{def:transport\text{-}values}\). The cited finite multi-marginal Kantorovich duality result \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}mot\text{-}kantorovich\text{-}duality}\) equates the minimum with its finite dual. Applying the same result to the negative cost and multiplying both primal and dual values by \(-1\) proves the corresponding equality for the maximum. Hence both programs give exact convexified empirical endpoints.

It remains to prove the replication assertion, which is specific to this proposition. The constraints in (2) have rational coefficients and rational right-hand sides. A linear functional on a nonempty polytope has an optimal face containing an extreme point; every extreme point of this rational polytope is rational because its coordinates solve a full-rank subsystem of the active rational equalities. Thus a rational optimal plan exists. More generally, let \(\pi\) be any rational optimal plan. Put \(N=\sum_am_{nba}=n_{nb}\), and choose an integer \(L\) divisible by \(N\), by every \(m_{nba}\), and by every denominator occurring among the finitely many values \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\). Create
\[
L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
\]
replicated units of joint type \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\). These multiplicities are nonnegative integers and sum to \(L\). By (2), the arm-\(a\) label \(i_a\) occurs exactly
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
=\frac{L}{m_{nba}}
\tag{3}
\]
times. Therefore, within arm \(a\), every label is replicated by the integer factor \(L/m_{nba}\), and the empirical joint law on the replicated common unit labels is exactly \(\pi\). Set the replicated complete-randomization quota to \(m_{nba}'=(L/N)m_{nba}\); these are positive integers, preserve the original arm fractions, and sum to \(L\). Assigning to each replicated unit the corresponding centered armwise residual values, and choosing fixed potential outcomes and nodewise predictable fitted values whose difference equals those residuals, realizes the plan at that single history node. Repeating the construction at integer multiples of \(L\) gives nodewise completion attainability along growing replicated block sizes. The construction neither retains the original unreplicated block size nor enforces compatibility with any other history node, exactly as the proposition states.

As the smallest arithmetic stress test, take both centered lists to be \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). For the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), equal-rank pairing makes the squared contrast identically zero, while reverse-rank pairing makes it identically four. Hence the two costs are \(0\) and \(4\), and for a block of size four the associated envelope width is
\[
\frac{4w_{nb}^2}{4-1}>0.
\]
For the normalized contrast \((1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and this width are divided by two. This verifies both the endpoint ordering and nontrivial width.

snapshot.stmt: The constructions in \(\text{def:twoarm-sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\) for \(K=2\). For each fixed \(K\), feeding the observable assigned-arm measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\) into the finite primal programs in \(\text{def:fixed-k-lp}\) attains \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\), and their Kantorovich duals have the same values. These are exact convexified empirical endpoints. At any single history node, every rational optimal plan is realized by a deterministic fixed-potential-outcome block completion after finite replication of that node's armwise lists, so its LP endpoints are asymptotically nodewise completion-attainable as block sizes grow. No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion that one \(\Xi_n\) realizes independently chosen nodewise plans, is made.

defs.def:fixed-k-lp: Feed the observable measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)}\) from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\) into the finite program. When every \(m_{nba}>0\), optimize over variables \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\), indexed by \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\), the objective \[\sum_{i_1\in\mathcal O_{nb1}}\cdots\sum_{i_K\in\mathcal O_{nbK}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\left\{\sum_{a=1}^Kc_a\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)\right\}^2\] subject, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), to the exact marginal constraints \[\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}.\] The minimum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and the maximum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\). If an arm sample is empty, represent its convention \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) by one artificial zero atom of mass one and solve the same marginal-coupling program; the admissible class never invokes this branch.
defs.def:observed-residual-margins:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).
defs.def:twoarm-sorting: For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), let \(F_{nb,a}^{-1}\) be the quantile function of \(\mu_{nba}\) and compute \[J_{nb}^{-}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(u)\}^2\,du,\qquad J_{nb}^{+}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(1-u)\}^2\,du.\]

assumptions.ass:predictable-adjustment: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:growing-arm-counts: The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).

thm:history-uniform-plugin.proof_tex:
Put \(p=4+\delta_0>4\), and fix a block \(b\), an arm \(a\), and an arbitrary pre-block history \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\). By \(\text{def:admissible-arrays}\), \(\text{ass:predictable-adjustment}\), and \(\text{ass:complete-block-randomization}\), the potential outcomes, adjustment values, residual lists, and quotas are fixed at this conditioning event, and the labels assigned to arm \(a\) form a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m=m_{nba}\) from \(N=n_{nb}\) labels. By \(\text{ass:consistency-no-interference}\), the observed residual on such a label is its fixed residual. Write
\[
X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad
\mu=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{X_i}=\mu_{nba},qquad
\nu=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i}.
\tag{1}
\]
Jensen's inequality and \(\text{ass:residual-moments}\) give the history-uniform centered moment bound
\[
H:=\frac1N\sum_i|X_i|^p
\le2^{p-1}\left\{\frac1N\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^p+|\bar R_{nba}|^p\right\}
\le2^pC_R.
\tag{2}
\]

Let \(C_T(x)=(-T)\vee(x\wedge T)\) for \(T\ge1\), and write \(\lambda^T=C_{T\#}\lambda\) for the pushforward of a measure \(\lambda\). We first control the bounded central part. If \(F_T\) and \(\widehat F_T\) are the distribution functions of \(\mu^T\) and \(\nu^T\), the exact first- and second-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling give, for every \(t\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat F_T(t)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}F_T(t)\{1-F_T(t)\}\le\frac1{4m}.
\tag{3}
\]
For finitely supported laws on the line, increasing matching gives
\(W_1(\nu^T,\mu^T)=\int|\widehat F_T(t)-F_T(t)|dt\): between consecutive ordered atoms, every plan must transport at least the cumulative mass imbalance across that cut, and increasing matching transports exactly that amount. Because both clipped laws are supported on \([-T,T]\), conditional Cauchy--Schwarz and (3) yield
\[
E\{W_1(\nu^T,\mu^T)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\le Tm^{-1/2}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\bar X_S=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\). The exact finite-population sampling-variance identity and (2) imply
\[
E(\bar X_S^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2\le C m^{-1}.
\tag{5}
\]
The observable measure is \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=T_{-\bar X_S\,\#}\nu\). Since clipping is one-Lipschitz,
\[
W_1(\widehat\mu_{nba}^T,\nu^T)\le W_1(\widehat\mu_{nba},\nu)=|\bar X_S|.
\]
Thus (4)--(5) and the triangle inequality give
\[
E\{W_1(\widehat\mu_{nba}^T,\mu_{nba}^T)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le CTm_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
All constants in this proof may depend only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,p,C_R\).

We next prove the tail estimate used below, including observable recentering. From overlap, \(m/N=p_{nba}\ge\varepsilon_0\), so every realized sample satisfies
\[
\int|x|^p,d\nu(x)=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}|X_i|^p
\le\frac NmH\le\varepsilon_0^{-1}H.
\tag{7}
\]
Jensen gives \(|\bar X_S|^p\le\int|x|^p,d\nu(x)\); hence
\[
\int|y|^p,d\widehat\mu_{nba}(y)
\le2^{p-1}\left\{\int|x|^p,d\nu(x)+|\bar X_S|^p\right\}
\le2^p\varepsilon_0^{-1}H.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus both the oracle and observable margins have a deterministic, history-uniform \(p\)-moment bound.

For later use, consider any \(K\) margins \((\lambda_a)_a\) satisfying \(\int|x|^p d\lambda_a\le H_0\), and let \(J^\pm(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K)\) denote the extrema of \(E(c^\top X)^2\) over their couplings. For any such coupling and \(X_a^T=C_T(X_a)\), expansion of the quadratic gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&|(c^\top X)^2-(c^\top X^T)^2|\\
&\quad\le\sum_{a,d}|c_ac_d|\left\{
|X_a|\mathbf1(|X_a|>T)|X_d|+|X_a|,|X_d|\mathbf1(|X_d|>T)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Hölder's inequality with exponents \(p,p,p/(p-2)\), followed by Markov's inequality, gives
\[
E\{|X_aX_d|\mathbf1(|X_a|>T)\}
\le H_0^{1/p}H_0^{1/p}\Pr(|X_a|>T)^{(p-2)/p}
\le H_0T^{-(p-2)}.
\tag{10}
\]
Contrast normalization implies \(\sum_a|c_a|\le\sqrt K\), so (9)--(10) show that clipping changes the cost of every coupling by at most \(2KH_0T^{-(p-2)}\). Clipping an original coupling gives a coupling of the clipped margins. Conversely, because these measures are finite, a coupling of the clipped margins can be lifted by drawing each original coordinate from its conditional empirical law given its clipped value. Applying the same bound to both directions and to minimizers and maximizers proves
\[
|J^\pm(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K)-J^\pm(\lambda_1^T,\ldots,\lambda_K^T)|
\le C H_0T^{-(p-2)}.
\tag{11}
\]
This is the required tail error; no optimizer uniqueness is used.

For margins supported on \([-T,T]\), the quadratic objective is Lipschitz in coordinatewise \(W_1\). Indeed, for \(x,y\in[-T,T]^K\),
\[
|(c^\top x)^2-(c^\top y)^2|
\le2T\|c\|_1\sum_a|c_a||x_a-y_a|.
\tag{12}
\]
Starting from any coupling of one set of margins, glue to each coordinate an optimal \(W_1\) coupling to the corresponding second margin. Equation (12), followed by the same construction in reverse, bounds the difference of both extrema by \(C_KT\sum_aW_1(\lambda_a,\widetilde\lambda_a)\). Apply this to the clipped oracle and observable margins, take conditional expectations, and use (6). Then use (2), (8), and (11) on both sides of this central comparison. For either sign,
\[
E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C\left\{T^2q_n^{-1/2}+T^{-(p-2)}\right\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Here count growth supplied \(m_{nba}\ge q_n\), and the fixed number of arms was absorbed into \(C\). Equation (13) explicitly separates the bounded central error from the moment-tail error.

The diagonal variance component is faster. Put
\[
A_S=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i^2,qquad A=\frac1N\sum_iX_i^2.
\]
Applying the same exact sampling-variance identity to the finite list \((X_i^2)_i\), and using the fourth-moment consequence of (2), gives
\[
E(|A_S-A|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\le Cm^{-1/2}.
\tag{14}
\]
For \(m,N\ge2\),
\[
\widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac m{m-1}(A_S-\bar X_S^2),
\qquad S_{nba}^2=\frac N{N-1}A.
\]
Equations (2), (5), (14), and the elementary bounds on the two finite-sample factors therefore imply
\[
E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le Cm_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]

Now take
\[
T=q_n^{1/(2p)},qquad
\kappa_\star=\frac{p-2}{2p}=\frac{2+\delta_0}{2(4+\delta_0)}.
\tag{16}
\]
For \(q_n\ge2\), this choice is admissible and balances the two terms in (13):
\[
T^2q_n^{-1/2}=T^{-(p-2)}=q_n^{-\kappa_\star}.
\tag{17}
\]
Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), so \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\). From overlap,
\(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), and for \(n_{nb}\ge2\),
\((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\). Combining (13), (15), (17), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and the two envelope definitions gives
\[
E\left[|\widehat L_{nb}-L_{nb}|+|\widehat U_{nb}-U_{nb}|
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right]
\le Ct_{nb}\{q_n^{-1/2}+q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\}
\le C't_{nb}q_n^{-\kappa_\star},
\tag{18}
\]
where the four symbols with subscript \(nb\) denote the corresponding block summands.

The bound (18) holds with the same constant at every possible pre-block history. Sum over blocks and apply the tower property under the original sequential randomization law; no maximum or union bound over blocks or histories appears. Since \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}
\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}q_n^{-\kappa_\star}
=C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n
\quad(q_n\ge2).
\tag{19}
\]
If \(q_n<2\), the loss in the theorem is truncated at one and
\(1\le2^{\kappa_\star}q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\); increasing \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}\) covers these total-convention cases. This proves the expectation bound for every \(n\).

For every nonnegative \(X\) and \(\eta>0\),
\(\mathbf1\{X>\eta\}\le(1\wedge X)/(1\wedge\eta)\). Applying this inequality to (19) proves the displayed probability bound. The Hausdorff distance between real intervals is
\(\max\{|\widehat L_n-L_n|,|\widehat U_n-U_n|\}\), which is bounded by the displayed sum, so it obeys the stated bound with the same constant. Finally, \(q_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa_\star>0\) imply \(r_n\to0\). Every conditioning step above is at \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\); none freezes \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every arm and block, form the observable assigned-arm measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}}\), centered by the observed assigned-arm residual mean \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}\), and feed exactly these measures into \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) and the plug-in envelope. There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), such that for every \(n\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n.\] Consequently, for every \(\eta>0\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta\right)\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge\eta}\longrightarrow0.\] The same bound, without the factor two implicit in the displayed sum, holds for the normalized Hausdorff distance between \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\) and \([L_n,U_n]\). Probability and expectation are over the original sequential randomization. The inequalities hold uniformly over pre-block histories generated by arrays in the common-parameter class, use observable assigned-arm centering throughout, and do not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) or freeze the realized final counts.

defs.def:admissible-arrays:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]
defs.def:observed-residual-margins:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).
defs.def:plugin-envelope: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]

assumptions.ass:complete-block-randomization: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).
assumptions.ass:growing-arm-counts: The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).
assumptions.ass:overlap: The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-adjustment: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:residual-moments: The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-potential-outcomes: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
assumptions.ass:predictable-counts: The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:block-leverage: The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
assumptions.ass:qv-growth: The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).

thm:conservative-wald.proof_tex:
Work on the subclass in the statement, on which \(\text{ass:qv-stabilization}\) holds uniformly in addition to membership in \(\mathfrak D\). Put
\[
p=4+\delta_0,qquad t_{nb}=\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}},qquad
s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}t_{nb},qquad \sigma_n^2=E_{\mathbb D}V_n.
\tag{1}
\]
First we connect the observed-data estimator to the fixed causal estimand. By consistency, on \(\{Z_{nbi}=a\}\),
\(Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)=R_{nbi}(a)\). Using
\(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\), \(Y_{nbi}(a)=g_{nbi}(a)+R_{nbi}(a)\), and
\(w_{nb}=n_{nb}/N_n\), direct subtraction in \(\text{def:aipw-estimator}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
&=\frac1{N_n}\sum_{b,i,a}c_a\left\{
\frac{\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}}{p_{nba}}R_{nbi}(a)-R_{nbi}(a)\right\}\\
&=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a
\left\{\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}\\
&=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Thus the equality is derived from the design and consistency, rather than imposed as a definition of the causal target. Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), predictable adjustment and predictable counts make every residual list and quota fixed. Complete-block randomization makes the arm-\(a\) labels a simple random sample of size \(m_{nba}\), whose sample mean has expectation \(\bar R_{nba}\). Hence
\[
E(D_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=0.
\tag{3}
\]

We derive the martingale Lindeberg condition from moments and leverage. Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\) be deterministic with \(\sum_ix_i=0\), let \(S\) be a uniform size-\(m\) subset, put \(A_r=\sum_i|x_i|^r\), and let \(\pi_r=(m)_r/(N)_r\), with \(\pi_r=0\) for \(r>m\). Expansion according to equality patterns among four sampled indices gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
E\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
={}&\pi_1A_4-4\pi_2A_4+3\pi_2(A_2^2-A_4)\\
&+6\pi_3(2A_4-A_2^2)+\pi_4(3A_2^2-6A_4).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
Indeed,
\[
\sum_{i\ne j}x_i^3x_j=-A_4,quad
\sum_{i\ne j}x_i^2x_j^2=A_2^2-A_4,
\]
\[
\sum_{i,j,k\ {
m distinct}}x_i^2x_jx_k=2A_4-A_2^2,quad
\sum_{i,j,k,l\ {
m distinct}}x_ix_jx_kx_l=3A_2^2-6A_4,
\tag{5}
\]
and these identities follow by expanding powers of \(\sum_ix_i=0\). Since
\(A_2^2\le NA_4\), \(\pi_r\le(m/N)^r\), and \(m\le N\), taking absolute values in (4) yields a numerical \(C_4<\infty\) such that
\[
E\left|\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right|^4
\le\frac{C_4}{m^2}\frac1N\sum_i|x_i|^4.
\tag{6}
\]

Apply (6), conditionally, to \(x_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\). Jensen's inequality, the power-mean inequality, and \(\text{ass:residual-moments}\) imply
\[
\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}|^4
\le16\left\{\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^p\right\}^{4/p}
\le16C_R^{4/p}.
\tag{7}
\]
If \(X_{nba}\) denotes the centered arm sample mean, contrast normalization gives
\[
\left|\sum_ac_aX_{nba}\right|^4
\le\left(\sum_aX_{nba}^2\right)^2\le K\sum_aX_{nba}^4.
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (6)--(8) with overlap, \(m_{nba}\ge\varepsilon_0n_{nb}\), gives a constant \(C_D=C_D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R)\) such that
\[
E(D_{nb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le C_D\frac{w_{nb}^4}{n_{nb}^2}=C_Dt_{nb}^2.
\tag{9}
\]
In particular, the martingale increments are square-integrable. Predictable-QV growth gives
\[
\sigma_n^2=E_{\mathbb D}V_n\ge v_0s_n^2>0.
\tag{10}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the inequality
\(x^2\mathbf1(|x|>y)\le x^4/y^2\), followed by (9), (10), and block leverage, yields almost surely
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac1{\sigma_n^2}\sum_bE\{D_{nb}^2\mathbf1(|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_n)
\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}\\
&\quad\le\frac{C_D}{\epsilon^2\sigma_n^4}\sum_bt_{nb}^2
\le\frac{C_D}{\epsilon^2v_0^2}\frac{\max_bt_{nb}}{s_n^2}
\le\frac{C_D}{\epsilon^2v_0^2}\ell_n\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Thus the conditional Lindeberg condition is derived from primitive design conditions. The additional stabilization assumption is precisely
\[
V_n/\sigma_n^2\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability, uniformly on the restricted class}.
\tag{12}
\]
Equations (3), (10)--(12), and the now self-contained
\(\text{lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation}\) give
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n}
=\frac{\sum_bD_{nb}}{\sigma_n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{13}
\]
Together with (12), the elementary continuity argument for products gives
\[
T_n:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
=\frac{(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n}{\sqrt{V_n/\sigma_n^2}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{14}
\]
For clarity, tightness of the numerator in (13) and convergence of
\((V_n/\sigma_n^2)^{-1/2}\) to one show their product difference tends to zero in probability; event inclusions at \(x\pm\eta\) then prove (14). The convergence is uniform: otherwise a sequence of arrays with a fixed distributional discrepancy would itself form a triangular array obeying the common constants and the uniform versions of (11)--(12), contradicting the proved pointwise limit.

It remains to compare the observable scale with the true predictable QV. The established \(\text{thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope}\) gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise. The sharpened \(\text{thm:history-uniform-plugin}\), with
\[
r_n=q_n^{-\kappa_\star},\qquad
\kappa_\star=\frac{2+\delta_0}{2(4+\delta_0)}>0,
\tag{15}
\]
gives, for every \(\eta>0\),
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}
\left\{\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta\right\}
\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge\eta}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Therefore, for every fixed \(\zeta\in(0,1)\), QV growth and (16) imply
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left\{\frac{\widehat U_n}{V_n}<1-\zeta\right\}
\le\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left\{\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\zeta v_0\right\}
\longrightarrow0
\tag{17}
\]
uniformly, because \(U_n/V_n\ge1\) and \(V_n/s_n^2\ge v_0\).

Let \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\). By \(\text{def:wald-interval}\), (14), and (17),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
&=\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|T_n|\le z\sqrt{\widehat U_n/V_n}\}\\
&\ge\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|T_n|\le z\sqrt{1-\zeta}\}
-\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\widehat U_n/V_n<1-\zeta\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
\]
Take the infimum over the restricted class and then the lower limit in \(n\). Uniform convergence in (14) and (17) makes the right side at least
\(2\Phi(z\sqrt{1-\zeta})-1\). Letting \(\zeta\downarrow0\), continuity of \(\Phi\) and the definition of \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\) give
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
\ge2\Phi(z)-1=1-\alpha.
\tag{19}
\]
All probabilities are under the original sequential assignment law; no step conditions on the terminal adaptive history.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), restrict attention to arrays in the displayed common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) for which \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) additionally holds uniformly. This is an explicit load-bearing high-level regularity condition and is not derived from predictable quotas, complete-block randomization, overlap, growing arm counts, leverage, residual moments, or QV growth. On that restricted class, \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] More precisely, the common leverage envelope \(\ell_n\to0\), the common residual-moment envelope \((\delta_0,C_R)\), the finite-population nondegeneracy condition \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\), together with this additional uniform predictable-QV stabilization, imply \((\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)/\sqrt{V_n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) uniformly. The nodewise rectangular envelope gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise, and the explicit bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n=o(1)\) permits \(U_n\) to be replaced by \(\widehat U_n\). No conditioning on the terminal adaptive path is required.

defs.def:admissible-arrays:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]
defs.def:plugin-envelope: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]
defs.def:observed-residual-margins:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).

assumptions.ass:block-leverage: The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
assumptions.ass:complete-block-randomization: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).
assumptions.ass:fixed-potential-outcomes: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
assumptions.ass:overlap: The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-counts: The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:qv-growth: The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).
assumptions.ass:qv-stabilization: For every \(\eta>0\), the predictable quadratic variation stabilizes at its deterministic design expectation uniformly over the common-parameter class: \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\left|\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}-1\right|>\eta\right)\longrightarrow0.\]
assumptions.ass:residual-moments: The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
assumptions.ass:predictable-adjustment: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
assumptions.ass:growing-arm-counts: The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).

When every \(m_{nba}>0\), optimize over variables \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\), indexed by \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\), the objective \[\sum_{i_1\in\mathcal O_{nb1}}\cdots\sum_{i_K\in\mathcal O_{nbK}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\left\{\sum_{a=1}^Kc_a\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)\right\}^2\] subject, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), to the exact marginal constraints \[\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}.\] The minimum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and the maximum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\). If an arm sample is empty, represent its convention \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) by one artificial zero atom of mass one and solve the same marginal-coupling program; the admissible class never invokes this branch.
