prose_overlay.tldr: Under predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete randomization within each growing block, past-only AIPW adjustment makes the centered block scores a martingale difference array. The paper's adaptive contributions are the nodewise-exact, pathwise rectangular predictable-QV transport envelope; an observable history-uniform endpoint bound of order \(r_n=q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\), where \(\kappa_\star=(2+\delta_0)/(2(4+\delta_0))\), over the general \(4+\delta_0\) moment class; the \(q_n^{-1/2}\) elbow on the bounded-residual subclass; and conservative martingale Wald coverage from the estimated rectangular upper endpoint under explicit predictable-QV stabilization. Two-arm sorting and a finite fixed-\(K\) transportation program make the endpoints computable. A globally consistent nonadaptive fixed-quota witness proves that no fixed fractional discount of the upper endpoint can retain uniform nominal coverage. No claim is made that one adaptive-history completion realizes independently chosen nodewise optimizers.
prose_overlay.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026), Section 5, Definition 2, allow arbitrary history-measurable joint block assignment laws with positive unit-level marginals, and Theorem 6 gives block-adaptive finite-population AIPW covariance, normality, and conservative coverage. The present predictable integer quotas followed by uniform fixed-count complete randomization are a narrower paper-imposed design whose covariance kernel admits the multi-marginal coupling analysis; Li--Zhao does not supply that kernel. Its Supplement Lemma S4 prints an indicator threshold that differs from the claim proved here, so that transcription is mismatch provenance only, while the present martingale CLT is proved by predictable stopping and characteristic functions. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) is used only as the bounded static i.i.d. transport plug-in benchmark; it does not prove either the general-moment history-uniform rate \(q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\) or the bounded-residual \(q_n^{-1/2}\) rate under finite-population sampling without replacement. Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014), Yu, Zhu, and Liu (2025), and Mikhaeil and Green (2024) provide static two-arm, nonadaptive-stratified, and regression-residual validation benchmarks. Ober-Reynolds (2023) studies i.i.d. empirical-process endpoint limits. Saco (2026) uses a different predictable-QV lower condition and realized-QV studentization. Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) and Hadad et al. (2021) provide adaptive inference under other assignment structures and normalizations. Harshaw, Middleton, and Savje (2026) optimize admissible quadratic bounds under general designs. Newby et al. (2025) is a motivating four-arm consumer, but application requires a predictably batched quota-controlled redesign rather than its original participant-level contextual bandit.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The rectangular relaxation permits a separate convexified residual coupling at every possible history node.  The exact-envelope theorem proves endpoint attainment at a single node and along any fixed path inside that rectangular product, but it does not prove that one fixed potential-outcome array and one predictable fitting rule realize independently chosen optimizers across all nodes of an adaptive history tree.  The fixed-fraction necessity theorem does not need that stronger compatibility: its equal-quota witness is nonadaptive, uses one globally consistent bounded potential-outcome array, and makes the true coupling attain the upper endpoint in every block.  Accordingly, the no-discount conclusion is certified for every broader family containing that subclass, while global adaptive-history completion sharpness remains outside the claim.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The adaptive contributions are the exact predictable complete-block transport envelope, the general-moment history-uniform endpoint rate \(q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\), the bounded-residual \(q_n^{-1/2}\) elbow, and conservative martingale coverage using the estimated upper endpoint under the separately imposed uniform predictable-QV stabilization condition. The CLT is derived from that stabilization, primitive moments, QV growth, and negligible block leverage; it is not assumed and does not use the mismatched Li--Zhao transcription. Predictable integer quotas followed by uniform complete-block randomization remain an explicit design restriction and are not broadened to arbitrary adaptive assignment laws. Exactness is nodewise and pathwise only in the rectangular convexified relaxation. The fixed-fraction necessity result uses one globally consistent nonadaptive fixed-quota completion, but no theorem claims that a single adaptive-history completion realizes independently chosen optimizers across different nodes. Gao--Ge--Qian is only the bounded static i.i.d. benchmark, and no minimax optimality claim is made for the general-moment exponent.

project_justification.gap: Existing adaptive AIPW limit theory does not supply the residual-coupling range created by predictable fixed-count complete randomization. Static transport results do not establish history-uniform finite-population plug-in control under outcome-adaptive future quotas. In particular, Gao--Ge--Qian is used only as a bounded static i.i.d. benchmark, not as support for the adaptive rate proof.
project_justification.niche: Predictable integer quotas followed by a uniform complete-block draw make each conditional variance summand a finite multi-marginal coupling problem while preserving a martingale across blocks. Under the common \(4+\delta_0\) residual-moment envelope, clipping at \(q_n^{1/(2(4+\delta_0))}\) gives the history-uniform rate \(q_n^{-(2+\delta_0)/(2(4+\delta_0))}\); a common absolute residual bound removes the tail term and gives \(q_n^{-1/2}\).
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the exact nodewise and pathwise rectangular QV envelope, computes it by sorting or a fixed-\(K\) linear program, proves the general-moment and bounded-residual observable endpoint rates without a block-count or history-union factor, and combines the upper endpoint with a proved martingale CLT and explicit predictable-QV stabilization to obtain conservative Wald coverage. A globally consistent nonadaptive fixed-quota sequence supplies the matching fixed-fraction no-discount certificate.

thm:conservative-wald.justification: The theorem combines the pathwise rectangular upper endpoint, the sharpened observable rate, and a derived martingale CLT to give unconditional conservative design-based coverage under explicit uniform predictable-QV stabilization.
thm:conservative-wald.gap: Existing adaptive-inference comparators use different assignment structures or studentizers and do not supply this finite-population complete-block residual-coupling endpoint with its history-uniform plug-in control.
thm:conservative-wald.consumer: A predictably batched quota-controlled multi-arm trial obtains valid contrast intervals when the displayed common design conditions and the separate predictable-QV stabilization condition hold.

thm:history-uniform-plugin.justification: The explicit general-moment rate \(q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\), with \(\kappa_\star=(2+\delta_0)/(2(4+\delta_0))\), is the observable bridge from the oracle rectangular envelope to adaptive inference.
thm:history-uniform-plugin.gap: The bounded static i.i.d. benchmark of Gao--Ge--Qian does not prove this predictable finite-population sampling-without-replacement result; the other adaptive comparators do not provide the residual-coupling endpoint.
thm:history-uniform-plugin.consumer: A batched multi-arm trial may estimate the endpoint whenever its minimum predictable arm count diverges, with no block-count, logarithmic history, leverage, or QV factor in endpoint estimation itself.

thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necess.justification: A bounded equal-quota sequence makes the true common-label coupling a zero-cost optimizer, hence \(V_n=U_n\), satisfies both endpoint-rate guarantees and all martingale conditions, and gives the exact strict undercoverage limit after a fixed discount.
thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necess.gap: The certificate closes fixed-fraction necessity on a globally consistent nonadaptive subclass; it makes no claim about simultaneous compatibility of independent nodewise optimizers on an adaptive history tree.
thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necess.consumer: Any broader design family containing the subclass cannot uniformly shorten the transport upper-endpoint standard error by a fixed fraction while retaining nominal coverage.

thm:bounded-residual-parametric-plugin.justification: The theorem identifies a parametric \(q_n^{-1/2}\) endpoint-rate elbow under a transparent optional history-uniform residual bound.
thm:bounded-residual-parametric-plugin.gap: The bounded-iid static benchmark does not establish the adaptive finite-population conditional-sampling result or justify integrating random future quotas by the tower property.
thm:bounded-residual-parametric-plugin.consumer: A quota-controlled batched trial with uniformly bounded nuisance-adjusted residuals obtains \(q_n^{-1/2}\) endpoint error with no \(B_n\) or logarithmic history penalty and no block-leverage requirement for this endpoint guarantee.

thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope.justification: This identifies the adaptive martingale normalization and its nodewise-exact rectangular range; the proof now obtains unconditional square integrability directly from the common residual-moment bound before using conditional complete-randomization identities.
thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope.gap: Existing adaptive covariance formulas do not characterize the predictable fixed-count complete-block residual-coupling range, and static transport formulas do not provide the history-tree rectangular scope.
thm:exact-predictable-ot-envelope.consumer: A predictably batched multi-arm trial can compute a narrow nodewise rectangular variance envelope for each prespecified causal contrast without conditioning on its realized terminal path.

lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation.justification: A predictable stopping and characteristic-function proof converts QV stabilization and the displayed conditional Lindeberg condition into Gaussian convergence.
lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation.gap: The proof is self-contained apart from the cited L\'evy continuity criterion; the mismatched Li--Zhao threshold is provenance only and supplies no logical premise.
lem:martingale-clt-predictable-variation.consumer: The lemma is the Gaussian-limit carrier for conservative adaptive Wald inference and the fixed-quota no-discount witness.

prose_overlay.interpretation: The observable interval estimates the range of the adaptive design's predictable quadratic variation that is compatible, node by node, with the armwise residual margins. It is exact in the rectangular convexified sense: at a fixed history node, and therefore along a fixed path when nodewise couplings are selected independently, both endpoints are attainable. This is not a theorem about one fixed potential-outcome completion simultaneously realizing choices on incompatible branches. The upper endpoint becomes a conservative standard error only under the separately stated predictable-QV stabilization condition, while the fixed-quota witness shows that a uniform procedure cannot discount that endpoint by a fixed fraction.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Armwise adjustments are fit only from past blocks and are held fixed during the current complete-block draw. Observable transport margins use assigned-arm residuals centered by their assigned-arm sample means. The common \(4+\delta_0\) moment envelope supports clipping and recentering at \(T=q_n^{1/(2(4+\delta_0))}\), while the optional history-uniform absolute residual bound yields the parametric \(q_n^{-1/2}\) endpoint rate.
sampling_model.uniformity: The number of arms \(K\), overlap and moment constants, deterministic lower count sequence \(q_n\), leverage envelope \(\ell_n\), and QV lower constant \(v_0\) are common across \(\mathfrak D\). Endpoint estimation is uniform at rate \(q_n^{-\kappa_\star}\), with \(\kappa_\star=(2+\delta_0)/(2(4+\delta_0))\), and uses neither block leverage nor a union bound over blocks or histories; leverage enters only the martingale Lindeberg argument for coverage.
sampling_model.design: Integer arm quotas are chosen from the pre-block history, after which assignments are uniform over allocations realizing those quotas. This implementable batched design is an explicit restriction of the broader adaptive assignment frameworks in the literature.
sampling_model.units: The data form a triangular array of fixed finite populations partitioned into growing, disjoint blocks; units are not sampled from a superpopulation.
sampling_model.treatment: There are a fixed number \(K\) of arms and a prespecified normalized zero-sum contrast \(c\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every executed predictable arm fraction obeys the same positive overlap constant \(\varepsilon_0\) over arrays and histories.
sampling_model.randomness: The only randomness is sequential treatment assignment; the potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.terminal_conditioning: All guarantees are unconditional under the sequential design and use only pre-block conditioning. The realized terminal adaptive path is never frozen, and rectangular nodewise attainment is not promoted to a globally consistent history-tree completion claim.
